Nidhi Gupta, J.

Present appeal has been filed by the injured injured-claimant seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.
Rs.46,000/- granted by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gurgaon (hereinafter referred to as "the learned Tribunal") vide Award dated 17.03.2015passed passed in claim petition bearing MACP Case No.21 of 2014 filed by the appellant/claimant under Sec Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") Act").
2.

Brief facts of the case are that the learned Tribunal on the basis of pleadings and oral &
documentary evidence adduced by the parties, came to the conclusion that the appellant/claimant was injured in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 22.06.2013 due to the rash and negligent driving of car bearing registration No.HR No.HR-12S-5080 (hereinafter referred to as "the offending vehicle") by respondent No.1.
Thee offending vehicle was owned by respondent No.2 and insured by respondent No.3.

The aforesaid compensation was awarded to the 1 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018065 appellant along with simple interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the petition till realisation payable by respondent respondents No.1 to 3 jointly and severally with costs.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation by submitting that in the accident in question the appellant had suffered 40% permanent disability.
The appellant had led sufficient medical evidence to prove this disability.
It is submitted that the appellant has become physically handicapped due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident and was placed in lower category of employment.
At the time of the accident, the appellant was only 24 years of age and has suffered great career loss.
loss Further, he would not be entitled to any promotion or annual increment and would be retired on attaining the age of 35 years only, resulting in huge financial loss losses.
It is accordingly prayed that the impugned Award be modified and the compensation paid to the appellant be enhanced.
4. No other argument is made on behalf of the appellant.
5. I have heard learned arned counsel for the appellant and perused the case file in great detail.

6. Briefly stated, the claim petition has been filed with the averments that on 22.6.2013, the appellant along with his friend Sumit Kumar, was going on the motorcycle bearing registration No.JH No.JH-02- R-6243, 6243, of his his said friend, from Signature Tower towards Maharana Pratap Chowk, Gurgaon.

At about 6.15 P.M when they reached at MDI U U- 2 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018065 turn, suddenly the offending car car bearing registration No.HR No.HR-12S-5080, being driven by respondent No.1 at a high speed, rash and negligent manner, came from behind and hit the motorcycle of the appellant, as a result of which the appellant and his friend fell down on the road.
The appellant received multiple injuries on on his leg and right hand and other parts of the body.
The appellant noted the number of offending vehicle as HR-12S-5080 5080 and thereafter the driver of offending vehicle ran away from the spot.
The appellant and his friend were admitted in Max Hospital, Gurgaon aon and after sometime the appellant was referred to Base Hospital, Delhi for further treatment in departmental ambulance.

FIR No.445 dated 23.6.2013 under Sections 279, 337 & 338 IPC was registered at P.S Civil Lines,
Gurgaon.

Respondent No.1 being the ow owner, respondent No.2 being the driver and respondent No.3 being the insurer of offending vehicle at the time of accident, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the claimant along with interest and costs.

7. At the time of accident, the appellant was stated to be 24 years old and was employed with Air Force Station, Sohna Road, Gurgaon, getting salary of Rs.25,000/-
Rs.25,000/ per month.
The appellant claimed to have sustained multiple injuries on his person person.

The appellantfurther claimed to have spent Rs.4,00,000/- on his treatment in Max Hospital, Gurgaon; Rs.50,000/-
Rs.50,000/ on transportation; Rs.50,000/ Rs.50,000/- on personal attendant and stated that the treatment is still going on.
Therefore, he 3 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018065 claimed an amount of Rs.70,00,000/-

sentences.text: I find no merit in the contentions raised by the appellant as the same are not supported by the evidence on record.
It has been contended by the appellant that in the accident in question, he had suffered 40% % permanent disability.

However, a p perusal of the record shows that in the accident in question, the appellant had suffered a fracture shaft distal 1/3rd tibia and fibula (right), which was surgically 'fracture corrected with closed reduction and internal fixation plus interlocking nail.'
There is nothing whatsoever on record to remotely indicate any disability let alone any permanent disability suffered by the appe appellant.
In support, the appellant had relied upon medical certificates (Ex.P4 and Ex.P5) before the learned Tribunal.

The appellant had examined 2 witnesses from his Department i.e. PW3 Dilbagh Singh who proved certificate of service (Ex.P1), summary of salary (Ex.P2); and PW44 S. Chatterjee, Junior Warrant Officer, who proved the medical certificates (Ex.P4 & P5) as per which permanent disability of 40% has been assessed assessed.

However, the said documents were rightly discarded by the learned Tribunal as the same could not be termed to be a "disability certificate" as the they were not issued by Medical Board;
Boar nor were they proved by a medical doctor doctor; nor same reflects the shortcomings on basis basis of which disability has been assessed assessed.
As such, except for the bald statement of the appellant, there was no evidence on record to prove any disability of the appellant.

4 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018065 9. It is also pertinent to note that as per Emergency Bill (Ex.P7), Max Hospital charged a sum of Rs.5,999.81/ Rs.5,999.81/- from the claimant;
and as per Discharge Slip (Ex.P8) the claimant remained admitted in Base Hospital, Delhi from 22.06.2013 to 08.07.2013.

However, the treatment of claimant was free of cost in Base Hospital,
Delhi sso compensation of Rs.6,000/- was awarded to claimant towards expenses incurred on medical treatment and medicines.

Further, an amount of Rs.5,000/ Rs.5,000/- was awarded to claimant towards expenses incurred on transportation and follow up treatment; and Rs.10,000/-
Rs.10,000/ towards expenses incurred on special diet.
An amount of Rs.25,000/- was awarded towards pain, suffering, frustration frustration.

As such, the learned Tribunal awarded compensation in the following manner:-

sentences.text: Further, there was nothing to indicate that the appellant had suffered any career loss.
There was no evidence that the appellant had been demoted from his service after the accident.
In fact, the learned Tribunal has recorded that the appellant continued tto serve in the Air Force Department, as was evident from his Salary Slip for the month of August, 2014 (Ex.P2).
The appellant also did not appear to have 5 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018065 suffered any adverse effects in his future career prospects due to his alleged disability.
11. It iss also relevant that as per salary slip Ex.P2 the claimant was getting gross salary of Rs.29,258/ Rs.29,258/- per month.

It has further been admitted by the claimant/PW1 PW1 in his cross cross-examination that no salary was deducted against leave period hence no compensation w was granted to him under head of loss of earning earning.
12. Learned arned counsel for the appellant is unable to dispute or controvert the aforesaid facts and findings.
13. Accordingly, in view of the discussion above, I find no case is made out that merits interference with the impugned Award.
I find the compensation awarded to the appellant to be just and fair in the facts and circumstances of the case.
No doubt Chapter Chapter-12 of the Act is a beneficial legislation yet, as cautioned by the Hon'ble Supreme Court Court, the same cannot be allowed to be treated as a windfall or a source of profit.
Moreover, compensation awarded upon mishap cannot be made a market negotiation, where every penny has to be calculated and drawn.

'State of Haryana & Another Vs. Jasbir Kaur & Hon'ble Supreme Court in 'State Others' Law Finder Doc ID # 64043 and 'Divisional Divisional Controller K.S.R.T.C. Vs. Mahadeva Mahadev Shetty',
(2003) 7 SCC 197, has held that the amount of compensation should be just and reasonable, it should neither be a bonanza nor a source of profit but at the same time it should not be a pittance.

sentences.text: Thus, all that has to be determined in the facts of a given case is, 6 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018065 that the compensation mpensation accorded is 'just'.

In my considered view, in the present case, the learned Tribunal has awarded a very 'just' compensation, which is in accordance with the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and therefore, does not warrant the interfere interference of this Court.

In case of 'KSRTC Vs. Susamma Thomas & Others' 1994 Volume-II II SCC 176, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that misplaced sympathy, generosity and benevolence cannot be the guiding factor for determining the compensation.
